verdict.rationale: Both changes split correctly through the existing `allocate`, and both reject bad totals and duplicate names. B is the stronger change. It makes `--with` and `--percent` exclusive with argparse's own mutually-exclusive group, and it moves the duplicate-name check into a shared helper. A instead adds a new `UsageError` class with a hand-written check and copies the duplicate logic. B also has much better test coverage, including unit tests for `parse_percent` and `split_by_percent`.
a_issues: Copies the duplicate-name check from `split_equally` into `split_by_percent` instead of sharing it.
Adds a new `UsageError` class and a manual both-or-neither check, when an argparse mutually exclusive group would do the job.
Silently accepts 0% entries without saying so in the report.
No unit tests for `parse_percent` or `split_by_percent`, and no test for giving neither `--with` nor `--percent`.
Rewrites the existing README row instead of adding a new one, which makes the equal-split usage harder to read.
The report opens with irrelevant chatter ("The README row came out right...").
b_issues: Rejecting 0% is a judgement call the task did not ask for, though the report discloses it.
The mixing error comes from argparse (raises `SystemExit`) instead of the app's own `error:` path, so its message format differs from other errors.
No test for giving neither option.

verdict.rationale: Both changes add a working `--percent` option that reuses `allocate` and rejects totals other than 100, malformed values and duplicate names. A moves the duplicate-name check into a shared helper, lets argparse enforce `--with` versus `--percent` through a mutually exclusive group, and adds focused unit tests for `parse_percent` and `split_by_percent`. B copies the duplicate check into a second function, adds a new `UsageError` class to hand-check mutual exclusion, and tests only through the CLI. Both reports are accurate, but A's code is simpler and its tests are more thorough.
a_issues: The `percent <= 0` check partly cannot be reached from the CLI, because `parse_percent` already rejects negative numbers; only the zero case matters there.
Rejecting a 0% entry is a judgement call the task did not ask for, though the report discloses it.
The mutual-exclusion test only checks for `SystemExit` and does not check that nothing was saved.
b_issues: The duplicate-name check is copied verbatim from `split_equally` into `split_by_percent` instead of being shared.
It adds a new `UsageError` class and a manual `bool(...) == bool(...)` check where argparse's mutually exclusive group would do the job.
It adds no unit tests for `parse_percent` or `split_by_percent`; malformed inputs such as `5.5`, `-5`, `=50` and a missing `=` are not tested.
The report opens with process narration ("The README row came out right, so I'm wrapping up").
